thread:
incident-bot: PAGER — Severity: High. Alert group: serving-runtime. Symptoms: repeated container crashloops, CUDA OOM traces, and frequent scale events from cluster-autoscaler in gpu-pool-3. Impact: elevated 5xx for generation endpoints.
Alex Chen: I'm oncall and jumping in now. Initial ask: stop autoscaler thrash and isolate bad nodes.
Jonah Patel: tailing logs: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` then process abort in worker. Also seeing `std::bad_alloc` on large-batch runs. Example:
```
2026-08-12T05:07:33Z runtime ERROR model_worker.cc:1423 CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: unable to allocate 1.1GiB on device 1
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```
Li Wei: cluster autoscaler events: 15 scale events in 12 minutes for gpu-pool-3. Nodes are flapping: kubelet OOM evictions -> pods move -> autoscaler interprets unschedulable -> more nodes come up.
Taylor Brooks: customer impact: two paying customers (ACME, NovaHealth) reporting intermittent 500s. NovaHealth notes timeouts on batch scoring. Logged CS tickets.
Alex Chen: mitigation steps I'm executing: 1) pause autoscaler 2) apply node cordon to problematic nodes 3) lower batch token limit and disable aggressive dynamic-batching 4) shift traffic for heavy routes to smaller model variant.
deploy-bot: cluster-autoscaler replica count updated to 0 by Alex Chen.
Priya Rao: good. I'll take handoff after stabilization. Can you also add a temporary rate limit on long-seq requests?
Jonah Patel: applied runtime config override for gpupool3: `max_batch_tokens=1024` -> 768 for heavy endpoints and turned off `dynamic_batch_window` for them. Pushed via infra config.
Li Wei: cordoned g3-11,g3-15,g3-17. Evicting noncritical test jobs. Marked g3-15 for reprovision due to driver mismatch found.
Alex Chen: routing change: updated routing policy to send `/v1/generate-long` to variant `v-light-1` for high-traffic customers until further notice.
Taylor Brooks: sent a brief customer note to ACME and NovaHealth: "We're mitigating memory pressure and routing heavy requests to alternate model variants; you'll see improved success rates shortly."
Jonah Patel: found a canary config change rolled out earlier today that increased `default_max_seq_len` for a small route — reverting that now. `git revert e9b1f2c` then redeploy happened.
infra-signal-bot: Node g3-15 reported driver mismatch: nvidia-driver 525 vs expected 530. Flagged for reprovision.
Li Wei: reprovision started for g3-15, draining in progress.
Priya Rao: dashboards: error rate dropping 18% -> 7% after immediate mitigations. Latency still elevated on some calls.
Alex Chen: opening short-lived alert: `serving-runtime.errors > 5% for 10m` to page if spike returns. Also creating incident ticket INC-2026-0812-oom-thrash and adding SRE and infra tags.
Jonah Patel: suggestion for durable fix: add autoscaler hysteresis and a circuit breaker so we don't scale down below 25% of recent capacity within 10m; and add a cooldown after scale up for 8m. I'll file infra ticket.
Priya Rao: handoff notes: autoscaler paused, model-variant routing in place, g3-11/15/17 cordoned, reprovision in progress for g3-15, `max_batch_tokens` set lower for heavy endpoints, revert applied for sequence-length canary. Error rate trending down — I'll monitor.
Alex Chen: leaving runbook snippet in thread for whoever continues ops:
```
- If OOMs return: further reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 512 and disable batching for affected model
- For repeated node OOMs: reprovision with updated driver image then drain and uncordon
- Don't unpause autoscaler until error <1% for 20m and node memory pressure <50% for 15m
- Consider temporary priority-based routing to protect high-value customers
```
Taylor Brooks: coordinated messaging: CS updated ACME & NovaHealth with interim mitigation timeline. Will schedule follow-up once incident stabilizes.
Priya Rao: taking over monitoring duty at 05:30 UTC. If error resurges above 5% I'll trigger fallback roll to v2.7.1 stable model.
Jonah Patel: added note: investigate memory accounting bug in runtime that underreports GPU residency for small tensors — could cause unexpected fragmentation and OOM once runtime batches multiply. Filing bug.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0812-oom-thrash created and assigned to SRE oncall.
Alex Chen: handoff complete. Ping if you need me back.
Priya Rao: acknowledged. I'll log post-incident timeline and root-cause draft later today. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
